segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Hi Chantal. What did you think of the talk, then?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Hi Hugo. I thought it was good once I’d moved seats.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Oh- were the people beside you chatting or something?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: It wasn’t that. I went early so that I’d get a seat and not have to stand, but then this guy sat right in front of me and he was so tall!

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: It’s hard to see through people’s heads, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Impossible! Anyway, to answer your question, I thought it was really interesting, especially what the speaker said about the job market.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Me too. I mean we know we’re going into a really competitive field so it’s obvious that we may struggle to get work.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: That’s right – and we know we can’t all have that ‘dream job’.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Yeah, but it looks like there’s a whole range of ... areas of work that we hadn’t even thought of – like fashion journalism, for instance.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Yeah – I wasn’t expecting so many career options.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Mmm. Overall, she had quite a strong message, didn’t she?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: She did. She kept saying things like ‘I know you all think this, but ...’ and then she’d tell us how it really is.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Perhaps she thinks students are a bit narrow-minded about the industry.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: It was a bit harsh, though! We know it’s a tough industry.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Yeah – and we’re only first years, after all. We’ve got a lot to learn.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Exactly. Do you think our secondary-school education should have been more career-focused?

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Well, we had numerous talks on careers, which was good, but none of them were very inspiring. They could have asked more people like today’s speaker to talk to us.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: I agree. We were told about lots of different careers - just when we needed to be, but not by the experts who really know stuff.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: So did today’s talk influence your thoughts on what career you’d like to take up in the future?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Well. I promised myself that I’d go through this course and keep an open mind till the end.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: But I think it’s better to pick an area of the industry now and then aim to get better and better at it.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Well, I think we’ll just have to differ on that issue!

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: One thing’s for certain, though. From what she said, we’ll be unpaid assistants in the industry for quite a long time.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Mmm.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: I’m prepared for that, aren’t you?

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Actually, I’m not going to accept that view.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Really? But she knows it’s the case- and everyone else says the same.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: That doesn’t mean it has to be true for me.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: OK. Well - I hope you’re right!

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: I thought the speaker’s account of her first job was fascinating.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Yeah – she admitted she was lucky to get work being a personal dresser for a musician. She didn’t even apply for the job and there she was getting paid to choose all his clothes.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: It must have felt amazing – though she said all she was looking for back then was experience, not financial reward.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Mmm. And then he was so mean, telling her she was more interested in her own appearance than his! _Q27/28_

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: But – she did realise he was right about that, which really made me think. I’m always considering my own clothes but now I can see you should be focusing on your client!

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: She obviously regretted losing the job.

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Well, as she said, she should have hidden her negative feelings about him, but she didn’t. _Q27/28_

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: It was really brave the way she picked herself up and took that job in retail. Fancy working in a shop after that!

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Yeah – well, she recommended we all do it at some point. I guess as a designer you’d get to find out some useful information, like how big or small the average shopper is.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: I think that’s an issue for manufacturers, not designers. However, it would be useful to know if there’s a gap in the market - you know, an item that no one’s stocking but that consumers are looking for. _Q29/30_

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Yeah, people don’t give up searching. They also take things back to the store if they aren’t right.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Yeah. Imagine you worked in an expensive shop and you found out the garments sold there were being returned because they ... fell apart in the wash! _Q29/30_

segments.speaker: CHANTAL
segments.en: Yeah, it would be good to know that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: HUGO
segments.en: Yeah.

Questions 21-30
TALK ON JOBS IN FASHION DESIGN
Talk on jobs in fashion design
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: What problem did Chantal have at the start of the talk?
    Options:
        Her view of the speaker was blocked.
        She was unable to find an empty seat.
        The students next to her were talking.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: What were Hugo and Chantal surprised to hear about the job market?
    Options:
        It has become more competitive than it used to be.
        There is more variety in it than they had realised.
        Some areas of it are more exciting than others.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: Hugo and Chantal agree that the speaker's message was
    Options:
        unfair to them at times.
        hard for them to follow.
        critical of the industry.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: What do Hugo and Chantal criticise about their school careers advice?
    Options:
        when they received the advice.
        how much advice was given.
        who gave the advice.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: When discussing their future, Hugo and Chantal disagree on
    Options:
        which is the best career in fashion.
        when to choose a career in fashion.
        why they would like a career in fashion.
    Q Num: 26
    Text: How does Hugo feel about being an unpaid assistant?
    Options:
        He is realistic about the practice.
        He feels the practice is dishonest.
        He thinks others want to change the practice.
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 27
Text: Which TWO mistakes did the speaker admit she made in her first job?

    Id: A

    Text: expecting to become well known
    Id: D
    Text: trying to earn a lot of money
    Id: E
    Text: openly disliking her client

Q Num: 29

    Id: C
    Text: fashion designs people want but can't find
